statuses.in-progress: Work is actively targeting this requirement.
statuses.verified: Acceptance criteria demonstrated; evidence field is mandatory.
statuses.rejected: Will not be done; rationale is mandatory.
statuses.deferred: Intentionally postponed to a later phase; rationale is mandatory.

requirements.description: The product is a native Windows desktop application.
acceptanceCriteria: Runs as a normal user-mode Windows process on the supported Windows versions decided in ADR-0002.
No browser runtime or web-view shell is required for the core interaction.
requirements.evidence: A native user-mode process: a Win32 overlay with GDI and OLE drag and drop, and .NET 10 worker processes; no browser runtime or web view (none in the code or the dependency matrix). Every run in this repository was on Windows 11 Pro 26200. The supported baseline (ADR-0002) is still an open owner decision, and Windows 10 is untested (docs/acceptance/2026-10-21-functional-v1.md).

requirements.description: V1 processes files locally and works fully offline.
acceptanceCriteria: All operations complete with the network adapter disabled.
No outbound network connection is opened by the application during normal use (verified with a network monitor).
requirements.evidence: No network API in the product code (static check: the only System.Net reference is a generated implicit using). At run time, 10 netstat samples during 1000 conversions found 0 TCP/UDP endpoints owned by any of the 10 WinTools processes seen. Not done: a run with the network adapter disabled, which would change system settings (docs/acceptance/2026-10-21-functional-v1.md).

requirements.description: The application does not require Administrator rights or UAC elevation.
acceptanceCriteria: Installs and runs for a standard (non-admin) user account.
No manifest requests elevation; no runtime code path triggers UAC.
requirements.evidence: Both manifests request asInvoker with uiAccess=false. No code path uses ShellExecute, a verb or elevation. The runs of the acceptance gate (the Explorer suite and the 1000-conversion network check) were started from a shell whose token is not elevated: WindowsPrincipal.IsInRole(Administrator) returned False there, and the WinTools processes inherit that token. Not done: an installer (none exists, DIST-001) and a run under an account outside the Administrators group (docs/acceptance/2026-10-21-functional-v1.md).

requirements.description: Core interaction: the user drags a file from Explorer or the Desktop, activates the app with a trigger while still dragging, a radial menu appears near the cursor, the user drops the file on an action, and the operation starts immediately.
acceptanceCriteria: Works with a drag started in Windows Explorer and on the Desktop.
The radial menu appears without the user releasing the mouse button.
Dropping on an action starts the corresponding job; dropping elsewhere or cancelling leaves the file untouched and Explorer's own drag behaviour unaffected.
requirements.notes: Spike 001 (2026-10-20, docs/research/2026-10-19-interaction-spike.md): Explorer-sourced drag → Space/Ctrl+Space/X1 → overlay → DragEnter → Drop with correct paths (1 and 3 files, Unicode): 44/44 drop cycles; Esc cancels cleanly. 'Explorer unaffected' supported by folder assertions for shell-source runs, by listings only for Explorer runs, with one unexplained window-switch incident open (evaluator finding 2). Not yet: release outside the ring with Explorer underneath (AC3), Desktop as source, product job start (no product code yet).
requirements.evidence: Explorer source verified end to end: Explorer end-to-end harness (tests/WinTools.EndToEnd, Release, 2026-10-21, judged against the host log): png 100/100 (before the evaluator fixes) and 30/30 plus 10/10 (after); jpg 20/20; escape 10/10; release outside the ring 10/10; unsupported file 10/10 plus 3/3; fast release at 0/10/25/50 ms 100/100 plus 10/10 at 0 ms, every DragEnter ending in an accepted drop; worker crash 3/3 (Debug). The Desktop source is not tested yet. Explorer runs of the current design (docs/performance/2026-10-21-hierarchical-menu.md, 2026-10-21): 71/71 cycles in 22 scenarios: commands run on drop; a release on a category, an unsupported file, Escape and leaving the ring run nothing. The Desktop as drag source is not yet run.

requirements.description: The activation trigger is an open engineering question; Ctrl alone must not be assumed. The chosen default must not interfere with Explorer's Copy/Move/Link modifier semantics.
acceptanceCriteria: ADR-0003 records the evaluated options (Space, Ctrl+Space, other combos, mouse buttons, others) with measured latency, reliability and interference results.
The chosen default does not change Explorer's drop effect when the user does not activate the wheel.
requirements.notes: ADR-0003 holds measured results for Space, Ctrl+Space, X1, middle button (rejected: shell cancels the drag), Esc and Shift-held. The default is Space (ADR-0003 accepted with amendments), configurable to F8-F12. The human feel pass and the elevated-source check (UIPI) are pending. 2026-10-23 (ADR-0003 amendment, owner field report): Ctrl and Shift held with the trigger no longer block it (WinTools only ever answers COPY); Alt+Space during a drag is refused with a toast. Evidence: ModifierTriggerTests (failing on 8836149, passing after) and Explorer runs with Ctrl-click, Ctrl+A and Shift-click selections held through the drag.

requirements.description: The activation trigger is user-configurable.
acceptanceCriteria: A settings surface allows changing the trigger; the change takes effect without restarting the application.
Invalid or conflicting triggers are rejected with an actionable message.
requirements.evidence: The settings window (WinTools.Settings.exe, ADR-0016) offers the activation key as a choice of the allowed keys only (Space, F8-F12), so an invalid or modifier key cannot be entered; a hand-edited invalid value is repaired to Space and logged. The change applies without restarting: the window saves atomically and raises the settings signal, the host reloads and changes the hook key at once. Tests: TriggerKeyChangeTests.A_new_trigger_key_takes_effect_at_once_and_the_old_one_stops_triggering, UiSurfaceTests.A_saved_change_reaches_a_listener_through_the_signal. Measured on the Release host: settings.reload with TriggerKey F9 logged 225 ms after the signal (docs/performance/2026-10-21-ui.md).

requirements.description: The radial menu is context-aware: it shows only operations valid for the dragged file, derived from a central capability system, not from format logic in view code.
acceptanceCriteria: A single capability resolver answers 'what operations are valid for this input?' and has unit tests.
The radial UI contains no per-format branching.
Adding a new format or operation requires no change to the radial menu architecture (demonstrated by adding one in a test).
requirements.evidence: CapabilityResolver answers the question (CapabilityResolverTests, CapabilityMatrixTests). RadialMenu.Build groups the resolver's answer by operation kind; the overlay paints a MenuView of labels only (no per-format branching). RadialMenuTests.A_new_operation_appears_without_any_menu_change adds an operation in a test and it appears with no menu change. Explorer runs of the current design (docs/performance/2026-10-21-hierarchical-menu.md, 2026-10-21): 71/71 cycles in 22 scenarios, every command reached through the menu the resolver built for the dragged files (single files of all five formats, mixed batches of 12).

requirements.description: The radial menu remains usable near any edge or corner of any monitor, at any DPI scaling, without hardcoded pixel offsets.
acceptanceCriteria: Manual protocol passes at 100/125/150/200% scaling and on a two-monitor layout with mixed DPI.
Placement is computed from the physical cursor position and the monitor work area.
requirements.notes: Spike 001: placement computed from physical cursor + work area, clamped correctly at all 4 corners and 4 edges at 125 % on one monitor, drop received at each. Finding: at corners the cursor starts outside the ring (design change needed). 100/150/200 % and mixed-DPI two-monitor runs not possible on this machine.
requirements.evidence: Placement is clamped to the cursor monitor work area and scaled by monitor DPI (RingGeometryTests). Measured at 120 DPI on one monitor only; the multi-monitor and mixed-DPI manual protocol is not run. Explorer: a trigger in the bottom-right corner of the work area, 3/3: the ring was clamped, nothing opened until the pointer had reached its centre, then exactly the wanted command ran (edge run, 2026-10-21).

requirements.description: The radial menu appears with imperceptible latency after activation.
acceptanceCriteria: Trigger-to-first-frame latency meets the budget in docs/performance/budgets.md (p95), measured with instrumentation, not by eye.
requirements.notes: Spike 001 (Release, 100 cycles, Stopwatch in hook callback vs a per-host paint proxy, not DWM presentation): hook→first paint median 11 ms / p95 ≈14 ms / max 29 ms (Win32), 7 / ≈18 / 36 ms (WPF); first show 25–60 ms. Lower bounds that sit well inside the < 50 ms p95 warm / < 120 ms first-use budget; the budget's ETW/DWM measurement is still required in the product.
requirements.evidence: docs/performance/2026-10-21-first-slice.md: trigger to painted overlay, warm p95 4.0-13.9 ms (budget 50), first activation 27-38 ms (budget 120), measured in the product host (Release) from hook timestamps. UI phase (layered, animated overlay; docs/performance/2026-10-21-ui.md): warm p95 9.1 ms, first activation max 14.8 ms over 22 Explorer scenarios with animations on.

requirements.description: Original files are never destructively overwritten by default.
acceptanceCriteria: After any job (success, failure, cancel, timeout, worker crash) the input file's hash is unchanged.
Output is written to a temporary location, validated, then moved into place.
requirements.evidence: Source hash unchanged after success, every failure code, timeout and worker crash: ConversionJobTests, WorkerProcessTests, plus every end-to-end cycle. Temp, validate, then no-overwrite rename: ADR-0005. No cancel path exists in this slice, so the cancel criterion is not demonstrated.

requirements.description: Filename collisions are handled safely (photo.webp, photo (1).webp, ...).
acceptanceCriteria: Existing files are never replaced; a unique name is chosen deterministically.
Unit tests cover existing-name, multiple collisions, Unicode names, and long paths.
requirements.evidence: ConversionJobTests.Existing_destination_is_never_overwritten, Destination_created_concurrently_is_not_overwritten, All_candidate_names_taken_reports_NoFreeOutputName, Unicode_spaces_and_emoji_in_the_name_are_preserved, Long_paths_beyond_MAX_PATH_work; OutputNamingTests.

requirements.description: A failed, cancelled or timed-out job never leaves an output that looks successful; temporary files are cleaned up.
acceptanceCriteria: After forced failure modes (kill worker, corrupt input, timeout, cancel) no partial output exists at the final path and no temp files remain.
The user sees an actionable failure state.
requirements.evidence: No final output and no temp file after a worker kill (crash and hang tests), corrupt input (truncated and damaged PNG/JPEG), timeout and failed validation: WorkerProcessTests, ConversionJobTests. The user sees an actionable failure state: a toast with the failure and its reason in plain words, counted per batch (ADR-0016, FeedbackTextTests, JobFeedbackTests). Missing: cancel, which does not exist yet.

requirements.description: The application is modular: UI, Windows integration, input/activation, drag-and-drop, core commands, file type detection, capability resolution, job management, conversion adapters, worker process, settings, logging, notifications, infrastructure.
acceptanceCriteria: Module boundaries are documented in docs/architecture and enforced by project references (UI cannot reference an engine package).
No single class or project contains the application.
requirements.evidence: Projects: Core (no Win32 or engine), Windows (integration), Host (composition), Worker (engine). Enforced by WorkerProcessTests.Host_assembly_does_not_reference_the_worker_assembly (also checks that Core references no product assembly). docs/architecture/product-architecture-proposal.md describes the boundaries, but as a proposal; it has not been brought up to date with what was built.

requirements.description: Conversion engines sit behind stable adapter interfaces and can be replaced without rewriting the application.
acceptanceCriteria: The image engine is reachable only through an adapter interface.
A fake adapter is used in tests, demonstrating substitutability.
requirements.evidence: The engine sits only in the worker behind the request/result contract (ADR-0007). A fake adapter in tests was deliberately not built (YAGNI; one engine).

requirements.description: Expensive or unsafe conversions run outside the main UI process; the main application survives worker crash, hang or out-of-memory where practicable; the UI never freezes.
acceptanceCriteria: Killing the worker during a job leaves the main app responsive and reports a failure.
A hanging worker is terminated at the job timeout.
UI thread shows no stalls attributable to job work (instrumented).
requirements.evidence: Worker crash and hang tests: the host-side client survives and reports structured failures; a kill-on-close job object holds every worker. Jobs run in worker processes, off the UI thread. Instrumented: overlay show and paint latency while a batch keeps every worker busy is p95 9.6 ms and max 13.3 ms (idle p95 11.8 ms), so there is no stall attributable to job work (docs/performance/2026-10-21-soak.md). Memory: a 1.5 GB per-worker cap and a commit-bounded pool (ADR-0015, ResourceLimitTests).

requirements.description: Jobs support progress, cancellation, timeouts and clear failure states.
acceptanceCriteria: Job state machine has unit tests for every transition.
Cancellation and timeout are exercised by lifecycle tests.
requirements.evidence: Timeout and structured failure states exist and are tested. Progress exists: WorkerClient reports each finished file and a batch still running after 450 ms shows a progress toast (JobFeedbackTests.Progress_counts_every_file_once_and_the_summary_carries_names_and_sizes). Missing: user cancellation.

requirements.description: The idle application is lightweight: near-zero CPU, no filesystem scanning, no polling, no preloaded engines.
acceptanceCriteria: Idle CPU and memory meet docs/performance/budgets.md, measured over 60 seconds with the app in the tray.
No periodic timers or filesystem watchers exist in the idle path (code review + ETW trace).
requirements.evidence: docs/performance/2026-10-21-first-slice.md: idle CPU 0.000 % over 60 s, 7.0 MB private, 30.2 MB working set, no worker while idle. No timers, polling or watchers in the idle path (evaluator review 2026-10-21). Re-measured after the UI phase (tray, sounds thread, settings-signal wait): idle CPU 0.000 % over 60 s, 9.1-9.3 MB private, 39.6-39.7 MB working set, no timers while idle (the toast stops its timers at rest) (docs/performance/2026-10-21-ui.md).

requirements.description: Performance budgets exist for idle CPU, idle memory, startup, radial latency, job start latency, UI responsiveness and installer size, and are measured rather than guessed.
acceptanceCriteria: docs/performance/budgets.md lists each target and its measurement method.
A benchmark result file exists for each budget before the prototype is called done.
requirements.notes: Proposed targets written 2026-10-19. Every budget except the installer/portable size has a benchmark file.
requirements.evidence: docs/performance/2026-10-21-first-slice.md covers idle CPU and memory, startup proxy, radial latency and job latency. Leak and UI stall: docs/performance/2026-10-21-soak.md. 10,000 overlay cycles and 3000 conversions, no growth (quarter medians; the detector catches an injected leak). The overlay shows and paints in p95 9.6 ms (max 13.3 ms) while every worker is busy, against a budget of 0 frames over 16 ms. Worker memory per operation: docs/performance/2026-10-21-worker-memory.md. Missing: the installer/portable size. No shippable artifact exists until packaging is decided (ADR-0008, DIST-001). As an indication only, a framework-dependent Release publish of the host is 14.1 MB, of which the WebP engine is 13.4 MB (docs/acceptance/2026-10-21-functional-v1.md).

requirements.description: All input files are untrusted; type is detected by content, converters are treated as vulnerable components, process launching never builds shell strings from file paths, and paths with spaces, quotes, Unicode and >260 characters are supported.
acceptanceCriteria: Malformed-file tests pass without crashing the main app.
No use of cmd.exe or string-built command lines (code review).
Path edge-case tests pass.
requirements.evidence: Malformed input fails cleanly in the worker without affecting the host: truncated and damaged PNG/JPEG, zero-byte, mislabelled, 60,000x60,000 header and oversized input (ConversionJobTests, WorkerProcessTests). No cmd.exe and no string-built command lines: the worker starts via ProcessStartInfo with no arguments (evaluator review 2026-10-21). Path edge cases: PathPolicyTests, long, Unicode and UNC naming tests.

requirements.description: Produced files are never auto-launched; macros or embedded executable content are never executed.
acceptanceCriteria: No code path calls ShellExecute/Process.Start on an output file without an explicit user action.
No Office automation or macro-capable engine runs in V1.
requirements.evidence: The only Process.Start in the product launches the worker executable; no code path opens, executes or shell-launches an output (evaluator code review 2026-10-21). No Office or macro-capable engine.

requirements.description: Every substantial third-party dependency is documented in a dependency/license matrix before adoption; no GPL/AGPL obligations enter the shipped product.
acceptanceCriteria: docs/architecture/dependency-matrix.md exists with one row per dependency and the fields listed in docs/engineering/rules/dependencies.md.
License review recorded for any engine (FFmpeg, ImageMagick, PDF, archive, LibreOffice, Office SDKs) before it is referenced.
requirements.evidence: docs/architecture/dependency-matrix.md has one row per package: purpose, licence and redistribution, binary size, maintenance and security history. The alternatives and the reason for the choice of the only engine, SkiaSharp, are in ADR-0006, which the matrix row relies on. SkiaSharp has its own licence review (no GPL/AGPL obligation found). Packages are pinned centrally, and `dotnet list package --vulnerable --include-transitive` reports none (2026-10-21).

requirements.description: The first prototype is deliberately small: JPG/PNG/WebP with Convert, Compress and Resize, whose purpose is to prove the interaction is excellent.
acceptanceCriteria: No other formats or operations are implemented before UX-001, UX-005 and UX-006 are verified.
A go/no-go review on the interaction is recorded before scope grows.
requirements.rationale: Superseded by the product owner's decision to grow the scope before the interaction criteria were all met: the functional V1 roadmap (2026-10-20, TASKs 0-6) added BMP and TIFF, rotate, metadata, info and batch. The criterion "no other formats before UX-001, UX-005 and UX-006 are verified" was therefore not kept; it was not met by evidence. The interaction is verified with Explorer as the drag source, on one monitor at 120 DPI (ADR-0014; docs/performance/2026-10-21-hierarchical-menu.md); UX-001 and UX-005 remain in progress. Pending the owner's confirmation of this status change.

requirements.description: Arbitrary 'anything to anything' conversion.
requirements.rationale: Not a requirement and technically unsound: semantic and layout-reconstruction conversions cannot be made reliable. Every conversion path must be classified and only reliable ones are offered (see brief §Document conversion warning).

requirements.description: Office/document conversion (Word, PowerPoint, PDF to Word, etc.).
requirements.rationale: Explicitly excluded from the first implementation; requires separate research of Office integration, Open XML, LibreOffice headless, dedicated libraries, with licensing and fidelity analysis.

requirements.description: Backend, server, database server, user accounts, cloud sync, payments, subscriptions, analytics, remote processing, AI functionality.
requirements.rationale: Not part of V1 by product decision; V1 is local-first and offline. Reopen with a new requirement if the product direction changes.

requirements.description: The experimental stage uses easy private installation (portable build or simple installer); public distribution effort waits until the interaction is proven.
acceptanceCriteria: ADR-0008 records the chosen packaging for the experimental stage with SmartScreen and signing implications.
A friend can install and run the prototype from a shared artifact without Administrator rights.
requirements.rationale: Packaging and sharing an artifact belong to the stage after functional V1. The owner has asked for no publishing yet, and ADR-0008 is still Proposed. Measured meanwhile: a framework-dependent Release publish is 14.1 MB, of which 13.4 MB is the WebP engine. Pending the owner's confirmation of this status change.

requirements.description: Microsoft Store distribution.
requirements.rationale: Not part of the initial experiment per the brief. Revisit after the prototype is proven.

requirements.description: A keyboard-accessible alternative exists for users who cannot hold a mouse drag and press a key at the same time.
acceptanceCriteria: An alternative path (e.g. select files in Explorer, press a shortcut, choose the action with the keyboard) reaches the same commands.
The overlay exposes its sectors to UI Automation.
requirements.rationale: Deferred beyond V1 (owner's V1 UI brief, 2026-10-21: "if a full UIA provider is too risky for V1, document it"). The overlay exists only during a mouse drag, which has no keyboard or screen-reader path, and a UI Automation provider runs on the overlay thread, where ADR-0001 measured multi-second UI Automation stalls. The keyboard alternative path is a new feature, not polish. What V1 does provide is recorded in ADR-0016: checked contrast, states not shown by colour alone, text of at least 11 px, reduced motion, sounds that can be turned off, and an accessible settings window.

requirements.description: Drags whose data object has no CF_HDROP (virtual files from zip folders, Outlook, browsers) are handled explicitly.
acceptanceCriteria: The overlay shows an explanation instead of empty sectors, or does not appear; nothing is written.
Behaviour is covered by a test with a non-HDROP data object.
requirements.evidence: Implemented: a data object without CF_HDROP yields no paths, so the ring shows "No actions" and the drop effect is NONE (FileDropTarget/HDrop). The test with a non-HDROP data object is still missing.

requirements.description: Folders included in a drop are handled explicitly in V1.
acceptanceCriteria: V1 rejects folders with an actionable message or processes only the supported files inside, as decided in an ADR; never silently.
requirements.evidence: A folder without an image extension gets no commands. A folder named like an image (x.png) gets a command and then fails with SourceNotReadable (logged, error sound). An actionable message and an ADR are still missing.

requirements.description: Cloud placeholders (OneDrive files-on-demand) are never hydrated by content sniffing or capability resolution.
acceptanceCriteria: Files with FILE_ATTRIBUTE_RECALL_ON_DATA_ACCESS or FILE_ATTRIBUTE_OFFLINE are not opened at DragEnter; the user gets an explicit reason.
A test covers the attribute check.
requirements.evidence: Capability resolution reads no file content (extension hint plus PathPolicy string checks only), so dragging never hydrates a placeholder. Conversion reads the file and hydrates it. The attribute check and its test are not implemented.

requirements.description: An unwritable output location (read-only folder, protected location, removable media removed) produces an explicit failure or a documented fallback, never a partial file.
acceptanceCriteria: Lifecycle test with a read-only output folder: job fails with an actionable reason, no temp file left behind.
requirements.evidence: ConversionJobTests.Unwritable_destination_folder_fails_without_touching_the_source returns OutputDirectoryNotWritable with no temp file left. The user now sees the reason: the result toast maps it to "The output folder cannot be written to." (FeedbackText.Reason; FeedbackTextTests.A_failure_gives_the_reason_in_plain_words_never_the_worker_text_or_a_path), shown without taking focus (ADR-0016).

requirements.description: Image decoding loads only Microsoft-provided WIC codecs selected from our own content sniff; third-party codecs installed on the machine are never fed untrusted input.
acceptanceCriteria: Decoders are created by CLSID or with vendor GUID_VendorMicrosoft; a test asserts the decoder vendor.
The threat model records the codec-loading risk.
requirements.evidence: Codecs are created by CLSID only (src/WinTools.Worker/Imaging/Wic.cs); CodecVendorTests asserts GUID_VendorMicrosoft for all four; docs/security/threat-model.md records the codec-loading risk.

requirements.description: Uninstall removes everything the app created outside the user's files.
acceptanceCriteria: After uninstall: no HKCU Run entry, no %LOCALAPPDATA% folder (or the user is asked about settings), no running process, no registered window classes left by a stale process.
requirements.rationale: Uninstall behaviour depends on the packaging decision (DIST-001, ADR-0008), which comes after functional V1. Today nothing is installed: the host writes only %APPDATA%\WinTools\settings.json (on save) and %LOCALAPPDATA%\WinTools\logs, and registers no Run entry. Since the UI phase the settings window may also write the HKCU Run value "WinTools" when the user turns on Start with Windows (ADR-0016); an uninstaller must remove it. Pending the owner's confirmation of this status change.

requirements.description: Remove metadata: a copy without EXIF, GPS, XMP or text metadata, with the pixels unchanged where the format allows.
acceptanceCriteria: JPEG, PNG and WebP keep only an allow-list of elements without re-encoding (everything else, including vendor chunks, C2PA and trailing data, is dropped); TIFF is re-encoded pixel-identically. ICC and the displayed orientation are kept.
The result is verified independently of the removal: the same displayed pixels, and a walk of the whole output finds only allowed elements; a file with nothing to remove reports NothingToDo.
Reachable from the radial menu in Explorer.
requirements.evidence: MetadataTests and MetadataAllowListTests (Core: C2PA/private/legacy PNG chunks, data after IEND/EOI/RIFF, comments between JPEG scans, vendor APP14, JFIF thumbnails, padded orientation EXIF, truncated input refused); MetadataOperationTests, MetadataHardeningTests, TiffMetadataTests (Worker). Reachable through Tools in the two-level menu (ADR-0014). Explorer: Tools → Remove metadata on a JPEG with a comment segment, 3/3, the output valid and without the comment (jpg-strip run, 2026-10-21).

requirements.description: Image info: format, size, DPI, transparency, bit depth, orientation and which metadata is present, without writing a file.
acceptanceCriteria: No file is written.
Reachable from the radial menu in Explorer.
requirements.evidence: MetadataOperationTests.Image_info_reports_facts_and_writes_nothing. Shown in a plain message box; reachable through Tools in the two-level menu (ADR-0014). Explorer: Tools → Image info 3/3, the box shown and no file written (png-info run, 2026-10-21).

requirements.description: Batch: one drop of many files runs one operation on each, with a result per file.
acceptanceCriteria: Only operations valid for every file are offered; up to 1000 files per drop.
Bounded parallelism; one corrupt file or a worker crash fails only that file.
Duplicate names never collide; an Explorer multi-selection works end to end.
requirements.evidence: BatchTests.Hundred_small_files_convert_in_parallel_with_one_result_each_in_order, One_corrupt_file_does_not_affect_the_others, Same_stem_in_one_folder_gets_distinct_outputs_even_in_parallel, A_worker_crash_on_one_file_fails_only_that_file; CapabilityResolver intersection tests. Explorer harness 'batch': 12 files 3/3 runs passed, 60 files 1/1 passed (job.done ok=60), 2026-10-21. PoolHardeningTests: cancellation reported as Cancelled, scattered crashes do not end a batch, failures in a row end the lane with the rest reported not run, a hang times out only its file with no temp left in the output folder.

requirements.description: Persisted settings: trigger key, output location, JPEG/WebP quality, resize defaults.
acceptanceCriteria: Versioned schema; invalid values repaired to safe defaults; atomic save; a corrupt file is moved aside; a newer schema is never overwritten.
The output folder and qualities are honoured by the worker.
requirements.evidence: AppSettingsTests (Core); SettingsStoreTests (Missing_file_gives_defaults_and_save_round_trips, Corrupt_file_is_moved_aside_and_defaults_are_used, Newer_schema_is_read_but_never_overwritten, Repeated_saves_leave_one_file_and_no_temp); SettingsHardeningTests (newer schema unparsable, other casing or as a string never moved or overwritten; folder or file in the way and read-only or locked file make Save return false with the old content intact; invalid output folder reported); BatchTests.Configured_output_folder_receives_the_outputs, Jpeg_quality_from_the_settings_changes_the_output. Evaluator findings of PR #4 fixed. No settings UI (UX-003).
